item.title: Dangote to Open IPO for Refinery Business Within Two Weeks
item.description: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote said an initial public offering for his refinery, Africa’s largest, will open within two weeks.

item.title: Record Cash Freezes India’s Key Funding Market for 90 Minutes
item.description: A record cash surplus in India’s banking system is driving away borrowers.

item.title: Healey Should Restore UK Fiscal Buffer, Bloomberg Economics Says
item.description: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey should seek to restore most of the UK’s fiscal buffer at his upcoming budget to win over the bond investors it needs to sustain its large debt pile, according to a new analysis by Bloomberg Economics.

item.title: Capcom, Kokusai Electric and JX Metals to Join Nikkei 225 Index
item.description: Video game developer Capcom Co. and chip gear maker Kokusai Electric Corp are set to join Japan’s Nikkei 225 Stock Average from Oct. 1, according to index provider Nikkei Inc.

item.title: Why Laser Beams Are the Hottest New Tech in Defense
item.description: Bloomberg Intelligence’s Wayne Sanders on the booming industry of directed energy weapon systems.

item.title: Odd Lots: Why Laser Beams Are the Hottest Defense Tech (Podcast)
item.description: Odd Lots: Why Laser Beams Are the Hottest Defense Tech (Podcast)【原文：Odd Lots: Why Laser Beams Are the Hottest Defense Tech (Podcast)】

item.title: Global Food Prices Jump to Highest Since 2022 as Risks Increase
item.description: Global food prices climbed in August to the highest since the end of 2022, as escalating geopolitical tensions and extreme weather deepen concerns over supplies from key producing regions.

item.title: Ferrexpo Takes a Step Off the Brink With $100 Million in Funding
item.description: Ferrexpo Plc, an iron ore miner in Ukraine working to stave off insolvency, raised about $100 million from investors through a long-awaited fundraising program that it had called essential for its continued survival.

item.title: Czech Inflation Quickens Toward Target as More Price Risks Loom
item.description: Czech inflation accelerated closer toward the central bank’s target as policymakers weigh persistent price pressures and the need for more monetary tightening.

item.title: European Stocks Muted Before US Data; VW Soars on Restructuring
item.description: European stocks posted muted moves as investors prepared for key US jobs numbers that will provide clues on the chances of a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike this month. Volkswagen AG shares jumped on plans for a sweeping restructuring at the carmaker.

item.title: World’s Biggest Money Managers Are Rebuilding Gold Positions
item.description: Some of the world’s biggest money managers have rebuilt their gold holdings after prices dropped, betting that long-term drivers of the precious metal will endure even as the US Federal Reserve takes a more assertive stance on inflation.

item.title: US Retail Diesel Hits Record as Hormuz, Russia Crises Stretch On
item.description: US retail diesel rose to a record, threatening to further spike energy-driven inflation as wars in Iran and Russia roil the market.

item.title: Thailand Puts 49 Data Centers on Hold Over Resource Strain
item.description: Thailand’s embrace of data centers hit a speed bump after the government suspended construction of 49 server farms as public concerns about the power-hungry facilities’ impact on communities intensify.

item.title: Kazakhstan Delivers Third Straight Rate Cut on Slowing Inflation
item.description: Kazakhstan cut its key interest rate for a third consecutive meeting after inflation in Central Asia’s largest oil producer slowed to the lowest level in more than a year, though policymakers warned the room for further reductions has narrowed.

item.title: Pimco Fund Beating 97% of Peers Cuts ‘Mag Seven’ to Bet on Asia
item.description: A top-performing fund manager at Pacific Investment Management Co. is betting the next winners of the AI boom will be found outside of crowded US Big Tech firms, turning instead to Asian equipment suppliers, Chinese financials and healthcare stocks.

item.title: Korea’s Memory Chip Lead Over China Set to Grow, Report Says
item.description: South Korea’s lead over China in memory chip production is expected to widen further thanks to an aggressive expansion of domestic facilities by Samsung Electronics Co. and SK Hynix Inc., according to the Bank of Korea.

item.title: German Factory Orders Rise for Third Month as Economy Recovers
item.description: German factory orders advanced more than anticipated for a third straight month as a revival in Europe’s largest economy gathered pace.

item.title: Japan Finance Chief to Survive Takaichi’s Reshuffle, Reports Say
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama is set to remain in her position in an upcoming cabinet reshuffle, according to local media reports, a decision that would back her handling of the economy, the currency and a restructuring of the budget process.

item.title: World Bank’s Mishra Pushes Back on Doubts Over India Growth
item.description: A range of high-frequency indicators show India’s economy is gaining momentum, World Bank Executive Director Neelkanth Mishra said on Friday, pushing back against skepticism over whether strong headline growth reflects conditions on the ground.

item.title: Novo Owner to Build $62 Million Quantum Chip Plant in Denmark
item.description: The foundation that controls Ozempic maker Novo Nordisk A/S is building a new quantum chip factory in Copenhagen as the global race to develop the emerging technology heats up.

item.title: Nepal Floods Ruin Merchants, Traders Ahead of Crucial Festival Season
item.description: The clothes Ashok Kumar Chaurasiya wore as he fled his textile shop in Nepal’s Trishuli Bazaar last week were almost all he has left after the floods.

item.title: Economists See Final ECB Hike Next Week in Split With Markets
item.description: Economists think the European Central Bank will raise interest rates next week but not beyond that, a far more dovish outcome than markets are currently betting on.

item.title: PNJ Taps Chairwoman’s Family for Loan After Diamond Scandal
item.description: Phu Nhuan Jewelry JSC, Vietnam’s largest listed jeweler known as PNJ, is securing a loan from the family of Chairwoman Cao Thi Ngoc Dung to rebuild its business after a national diamond-smuggling scandal battered the industry.

item.title: Ex-RBA Official Expects September Hike, 10% Drop in House Prices
item.description: Australia’s central bank is likely to deliver another interest-rate increase at its meeting later this month, according to a former senior Reserve Bank official, who also expects property prices will fall by about 10%.

item.title: Andreessen-Backed AI Startup Gimlet Is Valued at $3 Billion in New Round
item.description: The company, which helps divide AI tasks among different chips, raised $300 million in its latest round

item.title: India Says US Trade Deal Hinges on Preferential Tariff Rate
item.description: India will finalize a trade deal with the US once Washington offers tariff terms that give exporters an advantage over competitors, Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal said, signaling a key sticking point in protracted negotiations between the two countries.

item.title: Sharp Price Swings Prompt SEBI Review of India’s Closing Auction
item.description: Regulator may propose changes to the way settlement prices for equity derivatives contracts are calculated.

item.title: Bathla Crisis Puts Focus on $94 Million of Unsecured Debts
item.description: Bathla Group’s administrator gave a breakdown of known creditors for the first time as talks remain ongoing to stave off liquidation at the embattled Sydney property developer.

item.title: Congo Ebola Outbreak: Roche to Expand Testing Capacity in Ituri
item.description: Roche Holding AG plans to deploy new laboratory equipment in the epicenter of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s Ebola epidemic as authorities struggle to contain a virus that has repeatedly outrun the response.

item.title: Japan Ministries Seek Larger Budget as Fiscal Concerns Mount
item.description: Japanese ministries requested substantially more spending for next fiscal year, with some major items still unresolved and investors focused on how large the final budget will become, and how the government will pay for it.
